newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso falls to low of 29.75 to the dlr.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso falls to low of 29.75 to the dlr.

text.p: The Philippne peso fell to a low of 29.75 pesos at mid-day on Monday after a lull of almost two hours in the peso-dollar market.
But volume was still light at nine million dollars after two-and-a-half hours of trading.
The first deals were at 27.50/28 to the dollar in very thin volume of $5 million.
Philippine banks continued to be wary on Monday after the peso's de facto devaluation last Friday, traders said.
"The traders are just staring at their screens," one dealer said. "They don't want to be disturbed."
"It's still a jittery market," another said. "There is no liquidity coming from the Central Bank."
One dealer said banks were buying and selling dollars at 27.50/32 in trades outside the computerised peso-dollar trading system.
The peso fell 11.5 percent to 29.45 on Friday after the Central Bank announced it would allow the peso to move in a new, wider range.
